raw_text:
8-351M. MOS 351M--Human Intelligence (HUMINT) Collection Technician (HUMINT Coll
Tech) (Effective 202410)
    a. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21.
    b. MOS 351M. MOS 351M is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is 35M/USMC
0211.
    c. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    d. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
warrant officer MOS).
       (1) N7--Strategic Debriefer
       (2) 1D--Digital Media Collector
       (3) V4--Advanced Source Handler (Effective 20221001)
    e. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
               (b) Possess a security eligibility of TOP SECRET with eligibility for access to
sensitive compartmented information (SCI). For clearance requirements to attend training, refer
to the Army Training Requirements and Resources System (ATRRS).
               (c) IAW AR 11-6 Para 7-2b(2) MOS 351M is a language capable MOS.
               (d) Complete the Human Intelligence Collector Technician MI Warrant Officer Basic
Course (WOBC).
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
               (b) Complete the resident MI Warrant Officer Advanced Course (WOAC).
         (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1) and (2).
               (b) Complete Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
         (4) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1), f(2), and f(3).
               (b) Complete Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
    f. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
               (a) Plans and directs interrogation operations, source operations, debriefing
operations, screening operations, intelligence liaison operations, and HUMINT analysis.
               (b) Plans and directs HUMINT scheme of support to multi-domain operations.
               (c) Integrates cultural intelligence and analysis into HUMINT operations.
               (d) Serves as the principal advisor to the Command and staff on HUMINT operations,
training, policies, and procedures.
               (e) Performs and manages HUMINT support to the Military Decision Making Process
(MDMP).
               (f) Plans Army HUMINT architecture.
               (g) Requests, integrates, and employs external capabilities to support HUMINT
operations.
               (h) Performs duties of Operational Management Team Chief, Interrogation Control
Element Chief, HUMINT Collection Platform Chief, HUMINT Analysis Cell Chief, and HUMINT
staff officer in an S/G2X.
               (i) May oversee unit language training program.
               (j) Coordinates with external agencies as needed in support of HUMINT operations.
               (k) Conducts all HUMINT operations at every echelons IAW applicable laws,
policies, treaties, regulations, and unit SOP.
               (l) May serve as a HUMINT Team/Section Chief at any echelon.
               (m) May serve as OMT Chief.
              (n) May serve as BCT S2X HUMINT Tech.
        (2) CW3--
             (a) Directs and performs duties described in paragraph e(1).
             (b) Synchronizes and assesses interrogation operations, source operations,
debriefing operations, screening operations, intelligence liaison operations, and HUMINT
analysis.
             (c) Plans and directs HUMINT scheme of support to Army, Joint, and combined
operations.
             (d) Serves as the principal advisor to Army, Joint, and combined commands and
staffs on HUMINT operations, training, policies, and procedures.
             (e) Performs and manages HUMINT support to the Army, Joint, and combined
planning processes.
             (f) Plans, directs, and integrates HUMINT architecture.
             (g) May oversee command language training program.
             (h) Performs duties of HUMINT Operations staff officer in a G/J/C2X.
             (i) Conducts all HUMINT operations IAW applicable laws, policies, treaties,
regulations, and unit SOP.
             (j) May serve as an instructor at the WOCC, or at 111th MI BDE.
             (k) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
             (l) May serve as a Doctrine or Capabilities Developer.
             (m) May serve as an OC/T at a CTC or MCTP.
        (3) CW4--
             (a) Manages, directs and performs duties shown in paragraph e(1) and e(2)
             (b) Synchronizes and assesses interrogation operations, source operations,
debriefing operations, screening operations, intelligence liaison operations, and HUMINT analysis
in Joint and Combined environments.
             (c) Plans and directs HUMINT scheme of support to Joint and Combined operations.
             (d) Serves as the principal advisor to Joint/Combined commands and staffs on
HUMINT operations, training, policies, and procedures.
             (e) Performs and manages HUMINT support to the Joint and Combined planning
processes.
             (f) Plans, directs, and integrates Joint and Combined HUMINT architecture.
             (g) Performs duties of HUMINT Operations staff officer in a G/J/C2X.
             (h) Conducts all HUMINT operations IAW applicable laws, policies, treaties,
regulations, and unit SOP.
             (i) May serve as the HRC MI WO Assignments Manager.
             (j) May serve as the MI WO Proponent.
        (4) CW5 --
             (a) Manages, directs and performs duties shown in paragraph g(1), g(2), and g(3).
             (b) MI CW5s are proficient in the duties described in the duties paragraphs of one or
more MI WO MOSs.
             (c) Develops and integrates policy governing interrogation operations, source
operations, debriefing operations, screening operations, intelligence liaison operations, and
HUMINT analysis for Army, Unified Combatant Command (UCC), DoD, and National Agency.
             (d) Assesses and ensures readiness of Army HUMINT workforce.
             (e) Serves as the principal advisor to HQDA, UCC, DoD, and National Agency on
HUMINT operations, training, policies, and procedures.
             (f) May oversee Army, UCC, DoD, and National Agency language training program.
             (g) Performs duties of HUMINT Operations staff officer in a G/J/C2X, Senior Warrant
Officer Advisor, or the Army Senior HUMINT trainer.
                 (1) MI CW5s are branch technical experts and master-level technical and tactical
experts who perform the primary duties of technical leader, manager, multidiscipline intelligence
integrator, and advisor.
                 (2) Provide direction, guidance, resources, assistance, and supervision necessary
for subordinates to perform their duties.
                  (3) Provide leader development, talent and lifecycle management, mentorship,
advice, and counsel to enlisted Soldiers, warrant officers, and branch officers and have special
warrant officer leadership and representation responsibilities within their respective commands.
                 (4) Primarily support division, corps, echelons above corps, and major command
operations.
                 (5) Advise commanders and branch assignment managers on the assignments
and placement of Military Intelligence warrant officers world-wide.
                 (6) Provide essential advice to commanders on warrant officer issues and perform
other officer level duties as required consistent with senior staff officer responsibilities
             (h) Conducts all HUMINT operations IAW applicable laws, policies, treaties,
regulations, and unit SOP.
             (i) May serve as the Senior WO advisor in MOS immaterial (011A) billets based on
technical knowledge and understanding of Army and Joint doctrine.
             (j) May serve on the Army Staff.
             (k) May serve as a Capabilities Branch Chief.
             (l) May serve as the MI WO Proponent.
             (m) May serve as the CCWO of the MI Branch.
             (n) MI Senior Field Grade Warrant Officers must have competed the WO Senior
Service Education Course prior to nomination for specified CW5 billets.
   g. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
       (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
       (2) A physical profile of 222211.
       (3) Have normal color discrimination with corrected vision per one of the following three
categories of the good eye, bad eye categories: 20/40-20/70; 20/30-20/100; or, 20/20/400,
       (4) Have hearing wherein sound amplitude in one ear does not exceed 45 decibels at
frequencies 250, 500, 1000, and 2000 CPS (HZ) or 65 decibels at frequency 4000.
       (5) Qualifying Scores
       A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) – 120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) – 350
cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 120 lbs, and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 36 shuttles in Physical
Demands Category “Moderate” (Gold).
       (6) Authorized position titles are provided in tables 8-351M-2 and 8-351M--3. The following
grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2;
W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following
standards of grade tables:
           (a) Table 8-351M-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
           (b) Table 8-351M-3. Standards of grade TDA.
